- Confirm final launch date & cutover window
- Runbook ownership (play-by-play) and canary plan
- Rollback/fallback triggers and SLA exceptions
- Compliance evidence and retention window

- MAP spreadsheet attached: Redwood-MAP-v3.xlsx — contains milestone owners and dates.
- Runbook draft attached: runbook-draft.md — currently placeholder steps for pre-cutover, cutover, post-cutover verification.
- Outstanding risk: EU region capacity constraint during spikes (see risk row 7 in MAP).

1) Please confirm final go-live date (if May 23 still stands).
2) Samir — can you confirm whether PulseHealth requires a warmed canary (10% traffic) vs staged rollout?
3) Dev/Neha — can you own the runbook edits and compliance checklist respectively and post updates by 5/09?

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), runbook-draft.md (markdown)

Thanks — Laura

Laura — thanks for the note and the attachments (received). Quick responses inline: 

> Please confirm final go-live date (if May 23 still stands).
We are still targeting May 23 on our side. I will lock in the calendar after our 05/04 sync.

> can you confirm whether PulseHealth requires a warmed canary (10% traffic) vs staged rollout?
We prefer a warmed canary for the first 24 hours with 10% traffic, then staged ramp if no regressions. Can you confirm rollback latency expectations (how quickly Redwood can flip the routing)?

Also — I see the EU capacity risk. If the canary experiences rate limits, our plan B is to failover EU traffic to the US region which will increase latency. Please include that explicit fallback in the runbook.

I'll be on the 05/04 call and will bring Cecilia (ops) to verify telemetry and retention questions.

Thanks,
Samir

Notes from today's 05/04 sync (summary):
- Confirmed go-live: 2027-05-23. Cutover window: 2027-05-23 02:00-06:00 UTC.
- Canary approach: 10% warmed canary for first 24 hours, then staged ramp to 100% over 6 hours if smoke tests pass.
- Fallback strategy: EU->US traffic steering as immediate fallback. If fallback engaged, Dev will disable prefix caching and reduce batch sizes to maintain throughput.
- Rollback triggers: repeatable regression on >3 endpoints within 15 minutes OR CPU/GPU saturation >85% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Acceptance criteria: 15-minute smoke tests pass (latency and error-rate thresholds defined in runbook).

Action items assigned (owners & deadlines):
- Dev Patel: update runbook with steering commands + canary automation snippets (due 2027-05-09).
- Neha Kapoor: SOC2 evidence manifest + retention confirmation; confirm whether 90-day logs are required (due 2027-05-10).
- Ben Carter: finalize rollback-playbook.pdf with explicit command set (due 2027-05-09).
- Laura Bennett: coordinate final test schedule and post-cutover acceptance window (deliver calendar invites and checklist by 2027-05-11).

Attachments posted: cutover-checklist.pdf (high-level pre/post cutover checklist) — uploaded to shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-cutover-docs

Please review and flag edits inline in the shared runbook. We'll reconvene 2027-05-11 for the pre-cutover dry run (30m).

Laura
